title.rendered: Forget Not All His Benefits — Morning Devotional

excerpt.rendered: David commanded his own soul to praise — before the feeling arrived. A mid-week devotional on the spiritual discipline of remembering what God has done, and refusing to forget His benefits.

content.rendered:
Gospelbuzz Morning Devotional — Wednesday, April 8, 2026

Scripture for Today — Psalm 103:1–5

“Praise the Lord, my soul; all my inmost being, praise his holy name. Praise the Lord, my soul, and forget not all his benefits — who forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the pit and crowns you with love and compassion, who satisfies your desires with good things so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s.”
— Psalm 103:1–5 (NIV)

Today’s Devotional Message

David is talking to himself. And it is one of the most spiritually healthy things a person can do.

Praise the Lord, my soul. He is not describing praise that is already happening — he is commanding his own inner life to rise. He is instructing his emotions, his thoughts, his deep interior self to get into alignment with what he knows to be true. Before the praise comes the decision to praise.

And then he does something crucial: he lists what he is not going to forget.

Forgiveness. Healing. Redemption. Love. Compassion. Satisfaction. Renewal. These are not abstract theological concepts to David — they are the specific, concrete, personal benefits of knowing God. He has experienced every one of them. And he knows that if he does not actively remember them, he will forget them — because the human heart forgets quickly, especially when the next difficulty arrives.

This is why gratitude is a spiritual discipline, not just a feeling. Feelings of gratitude come and go. But the practice of remembering — of deliberately counting what God has done, naming it, speaking it aloud — this is something we choose, regardless of how we feel.

We are one week out from the cross and the empty tomb. It is tempting to let Easter fade back into ordinary life. The flowers in the church have already been taken down. The special services are over. Monday and Tuesday came with their usual pressures. By Wednesday it can feel like the resurrection was just a weekend event.

David’s antidote is exactly what we need today: sit down and make the list. What has God forgiven you for? What has He healed? What pit has He pulled you out of? What desire has He satisfied? What part of your life has He renewed?

When you make that list — really make it, not as a spiritual exercise but as an honest account of your own history with God — the praise that follows is not forced. It is the only reasonable response.

Praise the Lord, my soul. Forget not all His benefits.

Prayer for Today

Lord, I don’t want to forget. I don’t want to be the person who walks away from the Easter weekend and returns to worry and unbelief by Wednesday. So today I choose to remember. I am grateful for Your forgiveness — real forgiveness, not just permission to feel better about myself but the actual removal of my sin. I am grateful for every healing You have brought, every pit You have lifted me out of, every moment of renewal I have experienced. Today I praise You not because everything is perfect but because You are faithful. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Daily Declaration

“I will not forget what God has done for me. He has forgiven my sins, healed my wounds, redeemed my life, and satisfied my soul. Today I speak to my own heart: praise the Lord. Rise up and remember. He is faithful — and so my praise will be faithful too.”

📖 Further Reading — Related Scriptures

  • Deuteronomy 8:2 — “Remember how the Lord your God led you.” — The spiritual discipline of looking back with gratitude.
  • Psalm 77:11 — “I will remember the deeds of the Lord; yes, I will remember your miracles of long ago.” — When the present is dark, remember the past mercies.
  • 1 Thessalonians 5:18 — “Give thanks in all circumstances; for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus.” — Gratitude as a command, not just a feeling.
  • Ephesians 1:3 — “Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in the heavenly realms with every spiritual blessing in Christ.” — The theological ground of all Christian gratitude.
  • Psalm 34:1 — “I will extol the Lord at all times; his praise will always be on my lips.” — The posture of a heart that has not forgotten.
